title: Candidate Generation vs Ranking
interviewAnswer: Large recommenders usually use a fast high-recall candidate stage followed by a richer ranking model. Candidate generation narrows millions of items; ranking uses more expensive features on hundreds/thousands.
why: Candidate Generation vs Ranking appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Large recommenders usually use a fast high-recall candidate stage followed by a richer ranking model. Candidate generation narrows millions of items; ranking uses more expensive features on hundreds/thousands. Ranking can incorporate context/business constraints. Training-serving feature consistency matters. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: ANN retrieval finds 1000 candidate videos; a ranking model scores them using user, item and context features.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Candidate Generation vs Ranking make?
How would you validate or debug Candidate Generation vs Ranking in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
